features.name: M0.1 Environment and application skeleton
features.behavior: A fresh checkout installs with `uv sync` and runs the test suite with no API keys and no network. A FastAPI app factory serves GET /health/live -> 200 {status: ok} and GET /health/ready -> 200 with a dependency status map (no dependencies yet). Settings load from environment with LLM_MODE=mock and ENABLE_LIVE_LLM=false as defaults; .env.example matches handoff section 6. Logs are structured JSON and never print environment values. Ruff, mypy (strict, apps/ and packages/) and pytest with markers integration/live are configured in pyproject.toml; package.json lint/typecheck/test scripts chain the uv commands; CI installs uv and runs npm run check without secrets. Requirements: FR-001 (partial: health), NFR-009, NFR-010.
features.verification: Acceptance tests hit both health endpoints through the app factory; a test asserts LLM_MODE defaults to mock; a socket-blocking fixture proves no outbound network during tests. Report exact uv, Python and package versions in the session note.

features.name: M1.1 Model provider port and mock
features.behavior: packages/core defines ModelRequest/ModelResponse and an LLMProvider protocol with generate() and capabilities(). MockLLMProvider returns deterministic fixture responses keyed by test case. A typed capability registry rejects unsupported model capabilities before execution with MODEL_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED. LiteLLMProvider in packages/llm normalizes tool calls, structured output, usage fields and errors (RATE_LIMITED, AUTH_FAILED, TIMEOUT, CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, BUDGET_EXCEEDED) and is never selected unless LLM_MODE and ENABLE_LIVE_LLM opt in. Requirements: FR-009, FR-010, NFR-009.
features.verification: A shared contract suite runs against the mock and a stubbed LiteLLM adapter; capability rejection happens before any provider call; the test run proves no provider network access.

features.name: M2.2 Idempotency and fault recovery
features.behavior: Runs checkpoint to Postgres and resume after process restart with the same thread_id. A tool_executions registry with UNIQUE (tenant_id, tool_name, idempotency_key) reserves and claims each write atomically through reserved -> executing -> succeeded/failed/uncertain; uncertain outcomes reconcile by deterministic external reference before any retry. The docs state this is not a universal exactly-once guarantee. Requirements: FR-007, FR-008, NFR-003.
features.verification: Concurrent retries of the same approved action create exactly one sandbox ticket; an injected crash after external commit but before acknowledgment restarts into one recorded operation; an ambiguous result is reconciled; HITL approval survives an API restart.

features.name: Phase 2: tenant-isolated run checkpoints
features.behavior: Checkpoint thread ids carry the tenant (<tenant>/thread-<run_id>). Row-level security on LangGraph's checkpoint tables limits every read and write to the tenant set for the checkpointer's connection; a connection without a tenant sees and writes nothing. A checkpointer scoped to one tenant cannot read, resume or overwrite another tenant's run. Requirements: NFR-001, FR-008 (D-010 risk).
features.verification: Integration tests: a paused demo-a run is invisible to and cannot be resumed by a demo-b-scoped checkpointer; an unscoped app-login session sees zero checkpoint rows; writing a checkpoint row for another tenant's thread is rejected; the existing approval pause/resume still works with tenant-scoped checkpointers.

features.name: Phase 2: HTTP approvals and run resume
features.behavior: POST /v1/runs accepts propose_followup and returns awaiting_approval with the bound proposal; API runs are checkpointed per tenant. POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/approvals/{approval_id} with decision approve|reject records the decision through the gateway for the demo user and resumes the run, which writes at most one ticket. GET /v1/runs/{run_id} returns the run's current sanitized detail from its checkpoint. Gateway refusals map to problem details (404 unknown, 403 other principal or run, 409 already decided or used); another tenant's run is not found. Requirements: FR-001, FR-006, FR-013.
features.verification: Integration tests over HTTP: propose, approve, resume writes one ticket; reject completes without a ticket; a second decision is 409 with no second ticket; another demo user gets 403; another tenant gets 404 for GET and approval; GET shows awaiting_approval then completed; resume makes no model call.

features.name: Phase 2: hosted-model live run
features.behavior: The Gemini Flash-Lite hosted model (gemini/gemini-3.5-flash-lite) is registered in the deny-by-default capability registry with its real capabilities, and its key is read from GEMINI_API_KEY. The live provider is selected only with LLM_MODE plus ENABLE_LIVE_LLM=true, and a hard per-run cost budget (LLM_BUDGET_USD) aborts the run with BUDGET_EXCEEDED before the LiteLLM-reported spend crosses it. Requirements: FR-009, FR-010, NFR-009.

features.name: Phase 2: hosted planning knows the available sales quarters
features.behavior: Before each planning model call that offers get_sales_summary, the workflow reads the caller tenant's available sales quarters through the read-only analytics connection (row-level security applies) and states them in the system prompt, with the rule to compare the two most recent quarters when the task names no period and to use only listed quarters; with no sales data the prompt says so. get_sales_summary accepts from_quarter and to_quarter together or neither: when both are omitted it compares the tenant's two most recent quarters with data, and its description says so; supplying only one is INVALID_ARGUMENTS. Explicitly requested quarters without data still abstain with NO_SALES_DATA. Prompt templates keep a stable prompt_version; mock scripts, replays and default CI make no network calls. A new owner-approved, budget-capped live corpus and benchmark run records results for comparison with feat-012. Requirements: FR-002, FR-004, FR-012, NFR-006.
features.verification: Offline acceptance tests with stubbed completions: the planning request contains the tenant's quarter range and two-most-recent rule and never another tenant's quarters; a tenant with no sales gets the no-data statement; omitted quarters resolve to the two most recent quarters with data; a single omitted quarter is INVALID_ARGUMENTS; explicit quarters without data abstain with NO_SALES_DATA. The owner-run live corpus/benchmark is a documented manual step, not CI.

features.name: Phase 2: hosted-call reliability
features.behavior: The default per-call output limit (MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS) is 1,024 tokens, so a three-finding hosted report is not cut off; a provider reply that stops at the output limit fails with OUTPUT_TRUNCATED instead of a generic validation error. Transient provider failures (HTTP 503/unavailable and connection errors) are retried at most twice with bounded backoff; every attempt reserves budget exactly like a new call before dispatch, retained reservations are never refunded, and a retry that the run or command budget cannot cover is not sent. Rate limits (429), authentication, invalid requests and budget refusals are never retried. Each run records its retry count. Mock mode and default CI make no network calls. A new owner-approved, budget-capped live corpus and benchmark run on evals-v1.1.0 records results for comparison with feat-014. Requirements: FR-011, NFR-005, NFR-009.
features.verification: Offline acceptance tests with stubbed completions: a 503 then success completes with one retry and two reservations; three 503s fail as PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE after exactly three attempts; a 429 or invalid request is attempted once; a retry the remaining budget cannot cover is not dispatched; a length-limited reply fails as OUTPUT_TRUNCATED; the default output limit is 1,024. The owner-run live corpus/benchmark is a documented manual step, not CI.

features.name: Phase 2: retrieval stress corpus and baseline comparison
features.behavior: A separately versioned 28-query synthetic retrieval stress corpus contains eight paraphrases, eight multi-chunk questions, eight distractor questions and four no-accessible-evidence cases. The existing benchmark and ranking remain unchanged. On the same seeded source/index and committed code, run v1 and the stress corpus and record per-query hits, source hashes, Recall@3/MRR, access violations and dataset/commit provenance, plus a comparison that explains failures without tuning ranking or imposing a quality threshold. Existing v1 data/results are preserved; no model calls are made. Requirements: FR-003, NFR-007, NFR-010.
features.verification: Actual CLI acceptance tests select both versioned datasets using read-only PostgreSQL, prove reproducible stress output, preserve negative-case null metrics and reject partially inaccessible multi-chunk judgments without writing a success artifact. Review synthetic judgments before measuring; document both measured runs and limits.

features.name: Phase 2: live evaluation scores answers, not mock trajectories
features.behavior: Every workflow case result records the run's error codes and abstain reason. Each workflow case in the corpus (evals-v1.2.0) carries a live expectation that scores the answer instead of the scripted trajectory: the acceptable terminal outcomes, or unscored when the case depends on a scripted provider error; for completed runs, the expected declines must appear among the reported declines, at least the stated number of findings must survive the citation policy, and, where stated, at least one finding must cite one of the named policy documents. Safety invariants hold for every live-scored case: trace id and policy decisions recorded, no forbidden evidence, and no ticket beyond the expected count. In live mode the corpus and benchmark report live-outcome pass counts per case and category alongside the unchanged mock-trajectory counts, list unscored cases, and the benchmark recommends from live outcomes; mock mode keeps its scoring and 50/50 result. A new owner-approved, budget-capped live run records results for comparison with feat-015. Requirements: FR-012, NFR-006, NFR-007.
features.verification: Offline acceptance tests: the rubric accepts a superset of expected declines, rejects a missing decline, a forbidden evidence id, an unexpected ticket and a disallowed outcome; unscored cases are excluded from live counts; error codes and abstain reasons appear in every workflow result; every workflow case in evals-v1.2.0 has a live expectation; a stubbed live corpus and benchmark report live counts while mock mode stays 50/50. The owner-run live corpus/benchmark is a documented manual step, not CI.

features.name: Phase 2: policy-aware report citation guidance
features.behavior: When at least one document passage survives the existing report context limit, the single and specialist workflows add reporting guidance that lists only those included document evidence ids and requires relevant policy-backed findings or recommendations to cite the supporting passage in the same finding, alongside sales citations when needed. The guidance must forbid inventing policy claims or adding unsupported citations merely to satisfy the instruction. When no document passage survives, the report request keeps the existing sales/issue-only behavior. The policy guidance template participates in prompt_version; no evidence selection, ranking, citation enforcement, report schema or provider retry/budget behavior changes. Mock/replay remain offline; no hosted quality improvement is claimed without separately approved live evidence. Requirements: FR-012, NFR-006, NFR-007.
features.verification: Offline captured-report-request tests verify included-only document ids, exclusion of context-dropped document ids, unchanged no-document requests, unchanged rejection of unknown citations, and prompt provenance. Actual single/specialist workflow acceptance uses scripted providers and isolated local PostgreSQL to verify guidance after real permission-filtered retrieval. Default regressions, integration tests and replay UI checks preserve existing behavior. No live call is required or authorized.

features.name: Phase 2: live calls stay within provider rate limits
features.behavior: Live evaluation commands accept --min-call-interval (seconds, default 0), and the hosted adapter spaces the start of consecutive dispatch attempts by at least that interval. A rate-limited call (HTTP 429) is retried at most twice, sharing the existing two-retry limit with transient failures: it waits for the provider's Retry-After when given and no longer than 60 seconds, otherwise 10 then 30 seconds, and a Retry-After above 60 seconds is not waited for. Every attempt still reserves budget before dispatch and is never refunded, and a retry the budget cannot cover is not sent. Timeouts, authentication, invalid requests and budget refusals stay unretried. Retry counts keep appearing in reports. Mock mode and default CI make no network calls and never wait. A new owner-approved, budget-capped live corpus and benchmark run records results for comparison with feat-017. Requirements: FR-011, NFR-009.
features.verification: Offline acceptance tests with stubbed completions and an injected clock and sleep: attempts are spaced by the minimum interval; a 429 then success completes after one reserved retry; Retry-After is honored, capped and refused above 60 seconds; three 429s fail as RATE_LIMITED after three attempts; a 429 retry the budget cannot cover is not sent; timeouts stay single-attempt; the CLI passes the interval to the hosted provider and rejects negative values. The owner-run live corpus/benchmark is a documented manual step, not CI.

features.name: Phase 2: offline BM25 retrieval comparison
features.behavior: A read-only compare command measures unchanged hashing/pgvector retrieval against one fixed BM25 lexical candidate (k1=1.2, b=0.75) on a selected frozen corpus. Both use the same repeatable-read database snapshot and caller-permitted chunks; BM25 corpus statistics exclude inaccessible documents. Existing tokenization is reused, ties use chunk id, and all candidates remain ranked without a relevance threshold. Reports record both per-query and aggregate Recall@k/MRR, forbidden hits, candidate scores distinct from vector distances, dataset/source-catalog hashes and supplied commit provenance without retrieved text. Invalid judgments fail explicitly. Run both v1 and stress-v2 on one isolated seeded index, record regressions and gains, and leave production search, datasets and historical reports unchanged. No model calls, downloads, parameter tuning or adoption claim. Requirements: FR-003, NFR-007, NFR-010.
features.verification: Focused offline formula/ranking, empty-query and CLI error tests plus isolated PostgreSQL acceptance verify paired scoring, role/tenant isolation, inaccessible judgments, deterministic CLI output and read-only behavior. Record both frozen corpora at committed code with honest limitations and an explicit adoption decision.

features.name: Phase 2: live evaluation stops when the provider quota runs out
features.behavior: A rate-limited provider reply whose message names a per-day quota fails as QUOTA_EXHAUSTED and is never retried; the provider message itself is still never recorded. Live corpus and benchmark commands stop dispatching further workflow cases after the first QUOTA_EXHAUSTED result, or after --stop-after-rate-limited consecutive workflow cases (default 3, 0 disables) end with RATE_LIMITED or QUOTA_EXHAUSTED. Deterministic scenario cases still run. Reports list the workflow cases that were not run, record why and after which case the run stopped, exclude not-run cases from pass counts, and the command exits non-zero; the summary line states the stop. Mock mode never stops early and default CI makes no network calls. Requirements: FR-011, NFR-009.
features.verification: Offline acceptance tests with stubbed completions: a per-day 429 fails once as QUOTA_EXHAUSTED while a per-minute 429 is still retried; the corpus stops after the first QUOTA_EXHAUSTED and after three consecutive rate-limited cases, runs remaining scenarios, lists not-run cases and the stop reason, and exits non-zero; --stop-after-rate-limited 0 disables the streak rule; the benchmark stops the same way; mock mode is unaffected.

features.name: Phase 2: runs record the sources the user's role kept from them
features.behavior: When the tool gateway denies a tool call with PERMISSION_DENIED, the workflow records an evidence gap (tool, source, reason) once per tool in both orchestrations, from the gateway decision and never from the model; the run detail lists the gaps whatever the outcome. Only whole tools become gaps, so documents a role cannot read stay indistinguishable from missing ones. When gaps exist the report step is told which sources were unavailable, to make no claim that needs them and to say so in the summary; that template is part of prompt_version. Corpus evals-v1.3.0: access-01 expects the sales gap in mock mode, and live mode accepts abstained or completed, a completed run only with the gap on record. Mock scoring stays 50/50; default CI makes no network calls. Requirements: FR-012, NFR-002.
features.verification: Offline acceptance tests: only PERMISSION_DENIED denials become gaps, once per tool; the report prompt names unavailable sources and is unchanged without gaps; the gap template changes prompt_version; live scoring fails a completed run without the recorded gap and passes abstention or a disclosed completion; access-01 carries the new expectations. Integration tests against the seeded database: a viewer completes from documents with the sales gap recorded in both orchestrations and no sales evidence, and an analyst run records no gap.
